answer: Cut a shale sample thirty microns thin and its minerals speak in color. The registry slices one section per applicant, photographing its pigment map under crossed polarizers — angles no other slide repeats. A falcon courier carries the sealed case to its holder, one bird, one flight, logged. Each epoch the registry names a fresh angle; the holder turns the slide, photographs the new colors, files it. One extra fake costs $275 for its own slide and flight, with a 40-minute solo booking. Five thousand fakes need 5,000 slides, $1.375 million; one slide per chamber visit, forty falcons in all.
